title: A Five-Level Operational Maturity Framework for Machine Learning in Midstream Oil and Gas
content: Machine learning is increasingly applied to midstream oil and gas pipelines, yet reported performance rarely establishes readiness for field use. This narrative review organizes peer-reviewed and industry sources from 2015–2025 using a five-level operational maturity framework (sensing and detection, diagnosis, prediction, decision and optimization, and human-supervised closed-loop automation), defined by a rubric of decision authority, operator role, and the validation evidence each level requires. A second axis records where each study’s performance was demonstrated, from simulation to closed-loop use. Applications include leak and anomaly detection, defect and corrosion assessment, hard spots, pump cavitation, predictive maintenance, failure-risk modeling, scheduling, and digital twins. Cross-classifying the coded sources on both axes shows that validation realism does not keep pace with claimed operational responsibility. Peer-reviewed evaluations are concentrated at Levels 1–3 and rely largely on laboratory, simulated, or retrospective data; the only operational Level 4 example is a practitioner case, and no coded source demonstrates Level 5 closed-loop control. The corpus thus shows a validation gap at the lower levels and an evidence-coverage gap at the upper ones; beyond the performance shown in controlled evaluations, validation, transferability, and governance remain major unresolved barriers to deployment. A ranked agenda led by graduated field validation follows.
